# PastoralMind — [Member-care logistics / Protestant & Catholic clergy]
**Claim:** A clergy-side AI co-pilot that reads a pastor's own dictated or typed visit notes over time, extracts latent risk signals from the qualitative content (grief language, relational isolation, spiritual doubt cadence), and surfaces a prioritized "who needs a visit this week" queue — going meaningfully beyond the quantitative attendance/giving flags that every current pastoral-care CRM already ships.
**Why-now capability:** Long-context LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7+) capable of sustained semantic analysis across months of unstructured free-text notes — identifying escalating emotional or theological distress vocabulary, not just attendance zeros — became reliably available in 2024-2025. Voice-to-structured-note pipelines (Whisper-class STT + structured extraction) make dictation-to-insight feasible with no extra data entry.
**Mechanism / rationale:** The self-handicapped incumbent pattern: CareNote, Relius Pastoral Care AI, CoPastor, and Digital Pastor all flag members via quantitative signals — missed check-ins, giving drops, event absences. None analyze the content of pastoral visit notes, because doing so requires storing sensitive qualitative data that their horizontal church-management positioning makes liability-toxic at scale. A focused pastoral-notes product can make a narrow, defensible privacy promise (notes never leave the pastor's account, no cross-church aggregation, no AI training on pastoral data) that a horizontal CMS cannot credibly make while selling to 10,000 churches. Payer: the individual pastor or pastoral care director ($29-49/month); also denomination-level licenses to all clergy in a presbytery or diocese. The wedge deepens because each pastor's note corpus is proprietary — after 6 months the model knows a congregation's pastoral vocabulary, making switching costly.
**Novelty:** Every verified competitor (CareNote, Relius, CoPastor, REACH Church Connect) flags disengagement from structured behavioral data. None read the note where a pastor wrote "Jim mentioned his son stopped speaking to him again — third time this year" and weight that as a higher-urgency pastoral signal than Jim's attendance record. The qualitative-text semantic layer is unoccupied.
**Test:** Recruit 10 Protestant pastors for a 90-day closed beta. Pastors dictate post-visit notes as usual. PastoralMind processes notes weekly and produces a ranked care queue. At 90 days compare: (a) pastor-rated accuracy of queue vs. their own intuition ranking, and (b) number of at-risk members the pastor would have missed without the tool. Success: >70% of queue items rated "I should have visited this person" and >=2 cases per pastor where the tool surfaced a signal the pastor had not registered.
**Assumptions:** (1) Pastors will dictate/type notes if friction is low. (2) Qualitative note content contains statistically distinguishable distress signals. (3) Privacy architecture can be made credible to clergy. Crisis-safety gate: any note containing acute crisis language (suicidal ideation, domestic violence indicators) triggers an immediate human-only flag — no AI action, explicit prompt to call a professional resource. Doctrinal accuracy: the tool never interprets theology; it surfaces names and excerpts for human pastoral judgment.
